rationale: The workflow runs on every push to main and can be re-triggered while an earlier run is still in progress. Since it only writes the current repository description to Docker Hub (derived from github.event.repository.description), the latest run reflects the current state and an older in-progress run is superseded. Adding a concurrency group keyed by workflow and ref with cancel-in-progress cancels stale runs on the same branch/tag, preserving required coverage because the newest revision always runs to completion. This matches P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE (cancel superseded runs), whose preconditions hold (same workflow/branch, newer revision supersedes older checks) and whose contraindications do not (this is metadata update, not release/deployment work; grouping by github.ref isolates branches). No permissions are weakened, no secrets or network access are added, and no unrelated changes are made.
